title: From Zero to Hero
subtitle: Grow up in Hearthcross. Become the adventurer your choices create.

rules.note: Developmental checks use normal 5E total-vs-DC success/failure. From Zero to Hero then applies its house-rule growth result: success earns flexible development, failure earns an off-path Lesson Point, natural-20 critical success earns one extra flexible point, and natural-1 critical failure can redirect one already-invested point from the attempted ability into the lesson ability.

start.possessions: Ordinary clothing and household items justified by family/home. No adventuring package.

development.spendTiming: between resolved growth beats and before graduation
development.lessonRule: A Lesson Point is locked to an ability different from the attempted ability and chosen because the failed scene plausibly taught that lesson.
development.criticalFailureRule: In addition to its Lesson Point, move one already-invested Development Point from the attempted ability into the same lesson ability when possible. This can lower one ability and raise another, but never reduces total earned development or the 27-point graduation floor.
development.criticalSuccessBonusRule: Critical success earns one extra flexible Development Point. There is no artificial cap; the natural roll frequency is the limiter.

abilityGuide.DEX: Balance, sneak, climb, aim, or use precise hands.
abilityGuide.CON: Endure, protect through stamina, resist hardship.
abilityGuide.INT: Study, reason, engineer, recall, or solve.
abilityGuide.WIS: Notice, judge, empathize, track, or survive.
abilityGuide.CHA: Persuade, inspire, deceive, perform, or lead.

development.maturitySettlementRule: After all 21 base Development Opportunities are resolved, any stranded Lesson Points blocked by the 15 cap and any stranded partial invested progress that has not completed an ability increase may be converted into Flexible Maturity Points. Graduation is blocked until the pre-origin array has at least 27 point-buy value. Critical failures may redirect where development lands, but can never reduce the 27-point minimum.

village.name: Hearthcross
village.pitch: A river-crossing village built around an old black standing stone, a market square, two mills, and a road that carries more strangers every year.
changesOverTime: Businesses open, close, or change hands.
Mentors age and their responsibilities shift.
Rivals can become friends, enemies, lovers, or leave town.
Locations damaged or saved in earlier chapters stay changed.
The old Watchstone mystery becomes more visible each year.

locations.name: Crossmarket
locations.use: festivals, contests, trade, public arguments and emergencies

locations.name: The Common Green
locations.use: games, training, militia drills and community meetings

locations.name: Shrine of the Open Hand
locations.use: faith, healing, charity and moral choices

locations.name: Quill House
locations.use: letters, records, lessons and arcane study

locations.name: The Hearth River
locations.use: fishing, ferrying, floods, rescues and travel

locations.name: Alderwood
locations.use: hunting, animals, survival and hidden paths

locations.name: The Watchstone
locations.use: old village landmark; warm to the touch before major storms

npcs.name: Captain Orren Vale
npcs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, iron-gray hair, left knee stiff in cold weather.
npcs.voice: Short sentences; asks questions instead of giving speeches.
npcs.wants: Hearthcross able to defend itself without becoming cruel.
npcs.fears: Training another young person who dies for his mistakes.
npcs.secret: He knows the Watchstone once reacted to bloodshed on the old road.
npcs.change: Strong at age 12; hand tremor appears by age 16; fully retired by age 18.

npcs.name: Sera Quill
npcs.appearance: Ink-stained fingers, copper spectacles, sleeves always rolled.
npcs.wants: Preserve the village records and understand the Watchstone.
npcs.fears: Her curiosity will expose something the village cannot contain.
npcs.secret: She has copied fragments of a pre-village ward diagram.
npcs.change: Local clerk at age 12; recognized scholar by age 18.

npcs.name: Sister Elwen Marr
npcs.appearance: Weathered face, shaved temple, patched blue shawl.
npcs.voice: Gentle until someone uses faith as an excuse for cruelty.
npcs.wants: Keep the village generous when fear rises.
npcs.fears: The shrine becoming a weapon in local politics.
npcs.secret: She once heard a voice beneath the Watchstone during a vigil.
npcs.change: Takes on two young acolytes as the party ages.

npcs.name: Bram Alder
npcs.appearance: Lean, sun-browned, one sleeve usually dotted with beeswax.
npcs.voice: Long pauses; describes people the way he describes weather.
npcs.wants: Keep Alderwood healthy and the river clean.
npcs.fears: The road expansion will ruin the woods.
npcs.secret: Animals avoid a buried stone circle north of town.
npcs.change: Becomes increasingly protective of the woods as traffic grows.

npcs.name: Tavi Brindle
npcs.appearance: Small, immaculate coat, brass key-ring at the hip.
npcs.voice: Warm salesman's cadence; notices every missing detail.
npcs.wants: Build Hearthcross into a prosperous stop without losing its character.
npcs.fears: Being remembered as merely a shopkeeper.
npcs.secret: Sometimes opens sealed letters for the reeve.
npcs.change: Expands from stall to storefront by age 16.

npcs.name: Maela Venn
npcs.appearance: Dark curls tied with green cord, sharp herbal smell on her apron.
npcs.voice: Dry humor; gives instructions while moving.
npcs.wants: Train enough hands that emergencies do not depend on her alone.
npcs.fears: A winter sickness she cannot treat.
npcs.secret: Keeps notes on strange fevers that coincide with Watchstone heat.
npcs.change: Takes over the full shop after her aunt retires.

npcs.name: Wren Cask
npcs.appearance: Heavy leather apron, burn scar across one forearm.
npcs.voice: Laughs loudly; criticizes work, not people.
npcs.wants: Leave the village safer than she found it.
npcs.fears: A bridge or building failing because she cut a corner.
npcs.secret: The Watchstone rings faintly when struck with her oldest hammer.
npcs.change: Becomes head of major village works by age 17.

npcs.name: Reeve Corlan Pike
npcs.appearance: Tall, neat beard, spotless boots even in mud.
npcs.voice: Formal in public; exhausted in private.
npcs.wants: Order, trade and a good reputation with the district.
npcs.fears: A disaster that proves he was unprepared.
npcs.secret: He suppresses old reports of the Watchstone to avoid panic.
npcs.change: Can become trusted ally or entrenched opponent based on player choices.

npcs.name: Jory Fen
npcs.appearance: Round face, quick hands, silver tooth.
npcs.voice: Every sentence sounds like the start of a story.
npcs.wants: A full common room and no blood on the floor.
npcs.secret: Keeps a coded ledger of travelers who ask about the Watchstone.
npcs.change: His daughter begins managing the inn by the final chapter.

npcs.name: Kess Reed
npcs.appearance: Freckled, cropped hair, always one scraped knuckle.
npcs.wants: To be first at something that matters.
npcs.fears: Everyone leaving Hearthcross before she can prove herself.
npcs.secret: Her older brother is tied to petty smugglers.
npcs.change: Can join the militia, leave with traders, or become a local organizer.

npcs.name: Nima Bell
npcs.appearance: Long braids, bright scarf, notebook of sketches.
npcs.voice: Asks the question everyone else avoids.
npcs.wants: See the world and draw places no one in Hearthcross has seen.
npcs.secret: She has sketched symbols near the Watchstone that change after storms.
npcs.change: May leave for a season and return with outside knowledge.

npcs.name: Rusk Thorn
npcs.appearance: Thin grin, oversized coat, silver ring he claims he won.
npcs.voice: Makes bad ideas sound like favors.
npcs.wants: Money and respect without waiting for either.
npcs.secret: Runs errands for smugglers by age 15.
npcs.change: Can become criminal, informant, or redeemed ally.

npcs.name: Old Sable
npcs.appearance: White hair, traveling cloak patched with unfamiliar cloth, black walking staff.
npcs.voice: Soft and precise; rarely answers the first question directly.
npcs.wants: Observe whether Hearthcross remembers why the Watchstone was raised.
npcs.fears: The ward failing before anyone is ready.
npcs.secret: She is descended from one of the ward's original keepers.
npcs.change: Appears only some years; her identity becomes clearer over time.

npcs.name: Mara Hale
npcs.appearance: Flour on her sleeves, red kerchief, strong forearms.
npcs.voice: Direct, affectionate, impossible to distract when worried.
npcs.fears: Adventure taking them farther away than home can reach.
npcs.secret: She once planned to leave Hearthcross herself.
npcs.change: Treat as a template guardian; replace or personalize per PC.

chapters.title: The Runaway Cart
chapters.objective: Keep Crossmarket from becoming a disaster when a grain cart breaks loose during the Founders' Fair.
chapters.pressure: Three beats before the cart reaches the crowded river steps.

growthBeats.title: The snap
growthBeats.prompt: The cart's brake chain snaps at the top of Market Hill. What do you do first?

approaches.STR: Grab a side rail and wrench the cart toward the ditch.
approaches.DEX: Sprint ahead, climb aboard, and reach the brake lever.
approaches.CON: Brace a rope line and hold despite the pull.
approaches.INT: Spot which wheel or axle can be jammed safely.
approaches.WIS: Read the crowd and identify who is in greatest danger.
approaches.CHA: Take command and clear a path through the market.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: You redirect the danger and save someone who could not save themselves; gain +1 reputation with one witness.
outcomes.success: You reduce the danger enough for the next beat to remain manageable.
outcomes.failure: You cannot stop it cleanly; a stall is damaged or someone is separated, but the next character gets a new opening.
outcomes.criticalFailure: You are knocked down or trapped by debris; the group must rescue you while the cart keeps moving.

growthBeats.title: The crossing
growthBeats.prompt: The cart is now aimed at a narrow crossing crowded with children and animals.

approaches.STR: Heave a barrier into its path.
approaches.DEX: Use balance and speed to release the team animals.
approaches.CON: Keep a panicked horse from crushing someone despite kicks and strain.
approaches.INT: Work out a safer deflection angle using barrels and slope.
approaches.WIS: Notice a hidden side lane or frightened child's position.
approaches.CHA: Coordinate villagers into a fast rescue line.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: You create a clean escape lane and Captain Orren notices your judgment.
outcomes.success: You prevent the worst harm.
outcomes.failure: The crossing clears, but something valuable is broken or lost.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Your move worsens the tangle; mark a minor scar/bruise or relationship complication, then continue.

growthBeats.title: Aftermath
growthBeats.prompt: Someone cut the brake chain. The adults are shouting over each other while evidence is being trampled.

approaches.STR: Physically secure the cart and preserve the broken chain.
approaches.DEX: Slip through the crowd to follow the fleeing suspect.
approaches.CON: Stay on your feet through the chaos and help carry the hurt.
approaches.INT: Examine the cut and determine what tool made it.
approaches.WIS: Read witnesses and separate fear from what they actually saw.
approaches.CHA: Calm the market and get useful witness statements.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: You preserve decisive evidence and earn a strong lead toward Rusk's older associates.
outcomes.success: You preserve enough evidence to prove the break was deliberate.
outcomes.failure: The truth survives through a second clue, but the direct trail is lost.
outcomes.criticalFailure: An innocent person is briefly blamed or a relationship is damaged; another clue still proves sabotage.

chapters.choice: Do you tell the reeve everything, protect a peer who was nearby, or take the clue to a mentor first?
chapters.consequence: Sets the party's first reputation and changes who trusts them in later years.

chapters.title: Winter Without Wolves
chapters.objective: Find out why livestock are vanishing before frightened farmers organize a dangerous hunt.

growthBeats.title: Tracks in snow
growthBeats.prompt: The tracks look like wolves until they reach a fence and become confusing.

approaches.STR: Move a frozen obstacle to reveal the ground beneath.
approaches.DEX: Follow the lightest prints without disturbing them.
approaches.CON: Push through hours of freezing search.
approaches.INT: Compare stride, weight, and fence damage to rule out wolves.
approaches.WIS: Read animal behavior and the terrain.
approaches.CHA: Persuade angry farmers to delay the hunt long enough to investigate.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: You find both the true trail and a useful dropped item.
outcomes.success: You identify that people, not wolves, are involved.
outcomes.failure: You learn the truth but lose time or supplies.
outcomes.criticalFailure: You lead the group into thin ice or another hazard; recover with a complication.

growthBeats.title: The hidden camp
growthBeats.prompt: The missing livestock are feeding displaced families hiding beyond the old quarry.

approaches.STR: Help repair their collapsing shelter.
approaches.DEX: Approach unseen to learn whether they are dangerous.
approaches.CON: Endure the cold while giving up your own warm gear or food.
approaches.INT: Assess how much food the village can spare and make a workable plan.
approaches.WIS: Judge who is sick, frightened, or lying.
approaches.CHA: Negotiate with the families and the farmers.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: You solve an immediate need and gain a grateful contact.
outcomes.success: You keep the situation from turning violent.
outcomes.failure: A compromise is possible but costs the village or your family something.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Your words/actions inflame one side; Elwen or Bram prevents violence, but trust drops.

growthBeats.title: The choice
growthBeats.prompt: The reeve demands names before he agrees to help.

approaches.STR: Take responsibility and physically deliver supplies despite orders.
approaches.DEX: Sneak food out without revealing the camp.
approaches.CON: Accept punishment or hardship to protect someone else.
approaches.INT: Find a legal/recorded obligation the reeve cannot ignore.
approaches.WIS: Read what concession Pike actually needs to save face.
approaches.CHA: Argue publicly for mercy or construct a convincing cover story.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: You protect the families and shift village policy in their favor.
outcomes.success: You secure temporary safety.
outcomes.failure: Safety is won with a debt, fine, or damaged relationship.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The secret breaks badly; the families must move, but they survive and remain future contacts.

chapters.choice: Expose, shelter, relocate, or publicly sponsor the displaced families.
chapters.consequence: Changes the village's attitude toward outsiders and can reshape Kess, Pike, Elwen, and Bram.

chapters.title: The River on the Rise
chapters.objective: Save people and infrastructure during the worst spring flood in a generation.
chapters.pressure: Flood Level 0–3 rises after each unresolved beat.

growthBeats.title: The footbridge
growthBeats.prompt: The footbridge is twisting loose with two villagers stranded midspan.

approaches.STR: Haul the guide rope tight.
approaches.DEX: Cross the swaying rail and clip in the stranded villagers.
approaches.CON: Hold the anchor in freezing water.
approaches.INT: Calculate the strongest new anchor point.
approaches.WIS: Read the current and predict the next surge.
approaches.CHA: Direct rescuers and stop panicked relatives from overloading the bridge.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Both villagers and a crate of medicine are saved.
outcomes.success: The villagers are saved.
outcomes.failure: The villagers survive but the bridge or medicine is lost.
outcomes.criticalFailure: You are swept into a secondary rescue; gain a scar/gear loss, but the story continues.

growthBeats.title: The apothecary
growthBeats.prompt: Water reaches Venn's Remedies while patients are still inside.

approaches.STR: Carry patients or furniture to higher ground.
approaches.DEX: Move through a narrow roof route with supplies.
approaches.CON: Work repeatedly in cold water without stopping.
approaches.INT: Identify which medicines must be saved first.
approaches.WIS: Triage patients and notice hidden symptoms.
approaches.CHA: Organize neighbors into evacuation and salvage teams.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Save all patients plus a valuable medical cache.
outcomes.success: Save the patients and core supplies.
outcomes.failure: Save the people but lose important stock.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A patient worsens or a relationship strains because of a bad call; Maela stabilizes the situation.

growthBeats.title: The mill gate
growthBeats.prompt: A jammed mill gate is backing water toward homes.

approaches.STR: Force the gate mechanism.
approaches.DEX: Reach the release wheel from the slick exterior.
approaches.CON: Stay in dangerous water long enough to hold a repair in place.
approaches.INT: Diagnose the jam and improvise a fix.
approaches.WIS: Notice a safer overflow route.
approaches.CHA: Convince property owners to sacrifice part of the mill to save homes.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Water drops and the mill survives mostly intact.
outcomes.success: Water drops before homes flood.
outcomes.failure: Homes are saved but the mill suffers major damage.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The repair fails dramatically; evacuations succeed, but the mill is ruined and someone blames you.

chapters.choice: Which property, livelihood, or resource are you willing to sacrifice to protect people?
chapters.consequence: Permanently changes a village location and determines who owes the party a favor.

chapters.title: The Lantern Fair
chapters.objective: Enjoy Hearthcross's largest fair, then solve a theft without letting rivalry turn into a mob.

growthBeats.title: Choose your contest
growthBeats.prompt: Each character enters or assists with one fair event.

approaches.STR: Wrestling, hammer lift, or hauling contest.
approaches.DEX: Archery, balance course, juggling, or precision craft.
approaches.CON: Long-distance run, cold-water swim, or endurance task.
approaches.INT: Riddle table, repair challenge, or strategy game.
approaches.WIS: Tracking game, judging contest, or animal trial.
approaches.CHA: Storytelling, debate, music, or crowd leadership.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Win decisively and attract a mentor/contact or special mundane prize.
outcomes.success: Place well and gain local recognition.
outcomes.failure: Lose cleanly but learn something useful.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Fail spectacularly; gain an embarrassing nickname or rival beat, but also a memorable relationship hook.

growthBeats.title: The missing coffer
growthBeats.prompt: A visiting artisan's locked payment coffer disappears.

approaches.STR: Search heavy crates and physically inaccessible storage.
approaches.DEX: Shadow a suspect through the fair without being seen.
approaches.CON: Keep searching through the night without rest.
approaches.INT: Reconstruct who had access and how the lock was bypassed.
approaches.WIS: Read body language and notice who is afraid rather than guilty.
approaches.CHA: Question witnesses or bait the thief into revealing knowledge.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Recover the coffer and reveal the method plus an extra clue about the Watchstone buyers.
outcomes.success: Recover the coffer or identify the thief.
outcomes.failure: Recover most value, but the culprit escapes or someone innocent is accused first.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The wrong accusation explodes into a fight or social rupture; evidence later corrects it.

growthBeats.title: Rusk's offer
growthBeats.prompt: Rusk offers to return the last stolen item if the party keeps his smuggling work quiet.

approaches.STR: Intimidate him physically without attacking.
approaches.DEX: Steal or snatch the evidence from him.
approaches.CON: Outlast a dangerous chase or vigil.
approaches.INT: Prove his leverage is false using records or logic.
approaches.WIS: See what Rusk is genuinely afraid of.
approaches.CHA: Bargain, persuade, deceive, or publicly corner him.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Secure the item and a major secret while deciding Rusk's future.
outcomes.success: Resolve the theft on your terms.
outcomes.failure: Get the item, but owe someone or lose trust elsewhere.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Rusk escapes with leverage; the theft is still solved, but he becomes a stronger future complication.

chapters.choice: Turn Rusk in, recruit him as an informant, protect him, or let him leave Hearthcross.
chapters.consequence: Determines whether the party gains a criminal contact, bitter enemy, or redeemed ally.

chapters.title: The Hollow Light
chapters.objective: Investigate lights and voices around the Watchstone after a lightning strike exposes buried masonry.
chapters.pressure: Three nights before district officials seal the site.

growthBeats.title: The buried stair
growthBeats.prompt: A collapsed stone stair descends beneath the Watchstone.

approaches.STR: Shift fallen blocks safely.
approaches.DEX: Squeeze through and secure a rope route.
approaches.CON: Work in stale air and cramped conditions.
approaches.INT: Read the masonry and find the original access pattern.
approaches.WIS: Notice airflow, sound, and unstable sections.
approaches.CHA: Get official permission or convince adults to let the group assist.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Open a safe route and recover an intact ward fragment.
outcomes.success: Open a usable route.
outcomes.failure: Reach the chamber but trigger a collapse that costs time or gear.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Become briefly trapped or injured; rescue reveals another entrance.

growthBeats.title: The echo chamber
growthBeats.prompt: Whispers repeat the characters' own fears and memories.

approaches.STR: Break or move the resonant stone creating the effect.
approaches.DEX: Cross the chamber without touching resonant tiles.
approaches.CON: Keep functioning while the whispers attack your composure.
approaches.INT: Map the repeating pattern and identify its mechanism.
approaches.WIS: Separate real sounds/emotions from magical echoes.
approaches.CHA: Speak aloud to steady the group or answer the echo without surrendering to it.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Master the chamber and reveal a hidden inscription.
outcomes.success: Cross and learn the core warning.
outcomes.failure: Cross with a fear, scar, or relationship confession exposed.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Panic or trigger a ward pulse; the group escapes, but the village notices the Watchstone flare.

growthBeats.title: Sable's truth
growthBeats.prompt: Old Sable admits the Watchstone is a damaged ward, but refuses to tell Pike everything.

approaches.STR: Demonstrate you can physically help maintain the site.
approaches.DEX: Follow Sable unseen to discover where she keeps old tools.
approaches.CON: Endure a painful ward test meant to prove resolve.
approaches.INT: Compare Sable's story with Quill's records.
approaches.WIS: Judge which adult is hiding the most dangerous truth.
approaches.CHA: Persuade Sable, Pike, or both to cooperate.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Unite two factions and gain a direct mentor/heirloom clue.
outcomes.success: Gain the truth needed for later chapters.
outcomes.failure: Learn the truth but deepen the conflict between adults.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Trust collapses; a physical ward fragment provides the necessary clue anyway.

chapters.choice: Who should control knowledge of the Watchstone: the reeve, mentors, the whole village, or a smaller trusted circle?
chapters.consequence: Determines who has authority during the final crisis.

chapters.title: The Broken Watch
chapters.objective: Protect travelers and Hearthcross when armed raiders exploit a night the Watchstone goes dark.
chapters.pressure: Four rounds of crisis; raiders withdraw if their objective becomes impossible.

growthBeats.title: Alarm at the north road
growthBeats.prompt: A wagon limps into town with raiders close behind.

approaches.STR: Move barricades and pull the wagon to safety.
approaches.DEX: Scout or flank through side lanes.
approaches.CON: Hold a position under sustained danger.
approaches.INT: Identify the raiders' actual target from their movement.
approaches.WIS: Spot a hidden second group or safe evacuation route.
approaches.CHA: Rally militia and civilians into useful jobs.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Save the wagon and learn the raiders' objective before they strike.
outcomes.success: Save the wagon and prepare for the next threat.
outcomes.failure: Save the people but lose cargo or position.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Your position collapses; someone is hurt or captured, creating a rescue objective.

growthBeats.title: A job, not a brawl
growthBeats.prompt: The raiders are trying to steal a Watchstone fragment, not conquer the village.

approaches.STR: Hold the access point or wrest the fragment away.
approaches.DEX: Reach the fragment first or sabotage the raiders' route.
approaches.CON: Keep a defensive task going while wounded/exhausted.
approaches.INT: Disable the mechanism or use the site layout to deny access.
approaches.WIS: Predict the raider leader's next move.
approaches.CHA: Bluff, command, bargain, or split the raiders' morale.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Deny the objective and create a noncombat surrender/retreat opening.
outcomes.success: Deny or delay the objective.
outcomes.failure: The fragment is partly damaged or stolen, but the raiders can be pursued or negotiated with.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The fragment is taken; a marked trail and captured clue preserve the path forward.

growthBeats.title: Orren falls
growthBeats.prompt: Captain Orren is injured while another objective remains active.

approaches.STR: Carry or shield Orren while others act.
approaches.DEX: Reach him through danger and extract him.
approaches.CON: Keep pressure on the rescue despite fatigue or injury.
approaches.INT: Assess the injury and choose the safest extraction.
approaches.WIS: Recognize whether Orren is actually the priority or directing you toward someone else.
approaches.CHA: Coordinate the rescue and defense simultaneously.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Save Orren and the objective; he entrusts his heirloom path if relationship supports it.
outcomes.success: Save Orren or complete the objective without abandoning either need entirely.
outcomes.failure: Choose one cost: Orren worsens, property is lost, or raiders escape.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A harsh consequence lands, but no required future path is blocked; this choice permanently marks relationships.

chapters.choice: Who or what do you prioritize when you cannot save everything?
chapters.consequence: Determines mentor fate, heirloom eligibility, and village defenses at age 18.

chapters.title: The Night the Watchstone Broke
chapters.objective: Use six years of relationships, training, and choices to save Hearthcross when the damaged ward finally fails.
chapters.pressure: Ward Collapse 0–4. Each unresolved major beat advances it.

growthBeats.title: The village chooses
growthBeats.prompt: Panic spreads as the Watchstone fractures and old paths under town open.

approaches.STR: Lead physical defenses and rescues.
approaches.DEX: Move rapidly between threatened locations or carry messages unseen.
approaches.CON: Keep rescue/repair work functioning through exhaustion.
approaches.INT: Use six years of clues to identify the failure sequence.
approaches.WIS: Read the village's danger and choose who needs help first.
approaches.CHA: Unite rival adults and assign people to jobs.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The village acts as one; reduce Ward Collapse by 1 and gain a final relationship boon.
outcomes.success: The village organizes enough to proceed.
outcomes.failure: The plan works with a cost: one location begins the finale already damaged.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Two factions split; a trusted NPC still creates a workable route forward.

growthBeats.title: Three jobs at once
growthBeats.prompt: The ward needs a physical anchor reset, a pattern restored, and frightened people evacuated.

approaches.STR: Reset the anchor or hold collapsing structure.
approaches.DEX: Cross the unstable site to place a needed component.
approaches.CON: Remain in the dangerous zone to keep a task active.
approaches.INT: Restore the ward sequence from records and fragments.
approaches.WIS: Sense the correct timing/route or calm people one by one.
approaches.CHA: Command teams, negotiate cooperation, or keep a crowd moving.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Complete your job and create one local edge: one other character may gain Advantage on one later Level-0 check in this chapter. No permanent build benefit.
outcomes.success: Complete your job.
outcomes.failure: Complete it with injury, lost gear, or a damaged relationship/location.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Your job fails first, but a mentor/relationship earned earlier offers a costly recovery route.

growthBeats.title: Who you became
growthBeats.prompt: The final decision cannot be solved by adults alone. The party must choose what Hearthcross becomes after the ward.

approaches.STR: Commit to a protective physical sacrifice or reconstruction.
approaches.DEX: Execute a precise dangerous final placement or retrieval.
approaches.CON: Endure the ward's backlash long enough for others to finish.
approaches.INT: Rewrite/reconfigure the failing pattern.
approaches.WIS: Choose the humane/sustainable path after reading the consequences.
approaches.CHA: Persuade the village to accept a difficult future and lead the final act.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Resolve the crisis with an extra preserved resource, relationship, or heirloom awakening opportunity.
outcomes.success: Resolve the crisis and graduate to Level 1.
outcomes.failure: Resolve the crisis with a permanent cost recorded on the village and character sheets.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The crisis resolves through a fail-forward emergency option, but Hearthcross bears a major scar that carries into later adventures.

chapters.choice: Preserve the old ward, rebuild it differently, or end it and accept a changed village.
chapters.consequence: Locks the Level-0 campaign ending, village state, mentor/contact state, heirloom state, and the story carried into Level 1.

order: Apply legal 2014 race/species ability adjustments and traits.
Carry only explicitly allowed story/proficiency elements.
forbidden: 2024 origin feats unless an explicit separate house rule is enabled

order: Carry only explicitly allowed story/proficiency elements.

originLegacy.rawDefault: Narrative heirloom/contact only. No extra feat, ASI, proficiency, class feature, spell, or magic property.
originLegacy.heroicLegacyOptional: Optional house-rule campaign mode may add a bounded heirloom or other legacy after the GM explicitly enables it.
originLegacy.mentor: Persistent narrative contact; no automatic numerical bonus in RAW mode.

rawAudit.abilityArray: From Zero to Hero ability generation is a house rule. After all 21 base opportunities, the character is guaranteed a minimum base-array point-buy value of 27, with no pre-origin score above 15. Any spent critical-success bonus points may raise the array above 27 and must be labeled Heroic/house-rule.
rawAudit.proficiencies: Training/familiarity remains narrative until a legal 2014 race/background/class or 2024 species/background/class choice grants the proficiency.
rawAudit.heirloom: Heirloom remains mundane/narrative unless the selected ruleset or an explicitly enabled house rule grants a mechanical property.
rawAudit.mentor: Mentors are narrative contacts and grant no automatic numerical bonus unless an explicit house rule says otherwise.
rawAudit.mechanics: After the base ability array is frozen, all species/race, background, class, proficiency, HP, spell, feat, equipment, and later advancement rules must follow the selected 2014 or 2024 ruleset exactly.
